description: drive the engine from the front end to a target at start-up through its own Lua: frontend | campaign:new:<campaign>:<faction> | campaign:continue | campaign:<save> | battle:<preset>; empty = off
settle time between the first front-end Lua pump and the config autostart

battle camera setter (J43): wsp.cam_set(x, y, z, yaw, pitch) in the dev Lua bridge calls the active camera mode's own SetTargetAndPosition on the engine thread (engine_sites battle.camera_*); ctl.py cam reads the pose back with probes/cam_read.lua

campaign console (J15): fill the executor's empty external-handler slot with a forwarder to the campaign CLI (built with the exe's own ctor on the live campaign context), and the ctl verb console <line>|status|on|off; off = nothing read or written in engine memory and console lines refused
control channel: requests <dev.ctl_dir>\<id>.cmd, results <id>.done (ping, state, log, lua, waitfor, autostart, reset, exit; proxy/README.md)
the control channel's folder, outside the game folder (D25) so the uninstall stays byte-exact
file-redirection rule file (relative to the game folder or absolute): redirect / fail / add / movie-fail / movie-redirect lines, proxy/core/filerules.h; empty = none
file-open survey: every distinct path the exe opens, checks or lists (CreateFile, GetFileAttributes, FindFirstFile) into nullgame\logs\files.log, and every movie open in proxy.log
the engine's Lua loads the proxy (wrapper scripts served by a virtual pack, wsp table: poll, result, dev_config, report, vanilla); needed for scenes from Lua, lua commands, autostart and reset
ctl perf <seconds>: records the time between presents (p50, p99, max, frame count) and reports process memory (address space, commit, working set)
refuse the start-up movies at BinkOpen (the adapter's list; the engine treats a refused movie as finished); the front-end background is untouched
nullgame\state.json rewritten atomically about twice a second: launch id, frame, scene, Lua context, battle probe, memory, Lua reports

phase timeline: one UTC millisecond timeline per launch in proxy.log and nullgame\logs\timeline.json (process start, DllMain, Direct3DCreate9, device, first Present, every movie, front-end pump, autostart, loading, scene ready, exit)
J13: the target display is the one non-primary display whose adapter or monitor string contains this (case-insensitive); never an index or a DISPLAYn name

J13: put every game window on the virtual display and never on a real monitor (fail closed: no target, a wrong size or a fullscreen device = hide everything, write nullgame\headless_status.json, exit 2160); the watcher turns it on for every launch but visible=1 ones
J13: after a topology change with no target found, keep retrying (cloaked) this long before refusing
J13: after a display-topology change the window stays cloaked until the layout has been quiet this long on the re-resolved target
J13: the wanted back buffer and the exact size the target display must have, WxH (the watcher sets it with x_res/y_res)

J12 PC test hook: this many ms after start-up the proxy shows a 640x480 window at the primary's origin from its own thread and import, as a DLL's dialog would appear; the window sweep must hide it (proves fix 1b); 0 = off, dev only

J12 PC test hook: relocations run on the guard thread, which does not own the game window, so the guard's move is asynchronous as in a game that presents from a worker thread (proves fix 1a); dev only
d3d9 implementation the exports forward to: dxvk (stock DXVK, pinned by proxy/tools/fetch_dxvk.py) or system (the Windows d3d9); a missing DXVK falls back to system with a warning
DXVK d3d9 DLL, relative to the game folder or absolute; DXVK log, config and caches are redirected next to it (never the game folder)
0 = pure pass-through: the backend only (no exe guard, no crash capture, no patches); for isolating a problem to the proxy
exe-identity guard: 1 = an exe that is not the pinned build runs as plain pass-through; 0 = developer override, engine features on whatever the exe (warned at every start)
test key: 1 = take the pass-through path on a matching exe (notice file and log as for a real mismatch); wins over exe_guard=0
lowest level written to nullgame\logs\proxy.log: debug, info, warn or error

in-process minidump into nullgame\dumps: 0 off, 1 unhandled exceptions only, 2 also the first fatal first-chance exception (when the game replaces the top-level filter); WER LocalDumps is the out-of-process backstop; release value 2 because the game replaces the top-level filter after DllMain (fact the game.crash.toplevel_filter_replaced, J3)
runtime patch engine: apply the engine_sites patches in memory once the exe guard accepts the exe (all-or-nothing); 0 = check and log only
